source.title: NeuMoSync: End‑to‑End Neuromodulatory Control for Plasticity and Adaptability in Continual Learning
source.citation: Seyed Roozbeh Razavi Rohani et al., 2026
source.authors: Seyed Roozbeh Razavi Rohani; Khashayar Khajavi; Wesley Chung; Mandana Samiei; Mo Chen

record.file_problem: Full text is present. It includes the main paper and appendices; no apparent cutoff affecting the reviewed claim.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates accuracy while models learn tasks with randomly assigned labels, using continual-learning task sequences and average online task accuracy rather than the original studies’ supervised random-label fitting and test-error measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports random-label MNIST and CIFAR-10 results in Figure 2 and Random-label CIFAR-10 results in Table 2. It does not report zero training error or chance test error for a single random labeling in the original supervised setting. Other memorization results are adaptation metrics, not direct fit-error measurements.
record.test_reason: The study uses random-label memorization tasks to evaluate its continual-learning method. Its online accuracy and adaptation metrics do not establish whether standard networks reach near-zero terminal training error with unchanged hyperparameters. Performance averaged over learning cannot establish failure to eventually fit the labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors additionally conclude that improved adaptation arises primarily from knowledge transfer through learned modulation rather than greater intrinsic learning speed.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a modified global-modulation architecture and sequential tasks with newly randomized labels, and evaluates average online task accuracy. It does not reproduce the original fixed-label supervised fitting and test-error protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different outcomes across methods on random-label tasks; its main comparison uses individually selected hyperparameters for each method and benchmark.

fits_no_version.finding: NeuMoSync achieves higher average online accuracy than the compared methods on sequences of random-label MNIST and CIFAR-10 tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Global modulation improves continual memorization performance and preserves plasticity under the tested training budgets.

record.problems: The random-label results are from continual sequences with labels randomized for each task, and are reported as average online task accuracy rather than training and test error for a fixed random labeling. Figure 2 has no exact values in its accompanying text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports adaptation and knowledge-transfer metrics for random-label tasks, not fitting error, so those results were not extracted as V1 rows. Figure 2 includes curves for multiple baselines, but exact values are not stated; rows here retain the explicitly described NeuMoSync outcome rather than reconstructing values from the plot.

untested.parts: Near-zero terminal training error on completely random labels for standard networks; chance test error; fitting without architecture or hyperparameter changes.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases. Method runtime comparisons do not test these predictions.

Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Permuted MNIST uses a shared permutation within each task, but its restricted-budget performance does not establish zero-error fitting. V3 does not require random labels.
A corruption-fraction sweep establishing perfect training fit alongside steadily worsening test error.

Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent complete random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization. Regularization baselines and augmentation in method comparisons do not establish these effects.
Within-training ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V1 limits_scope verdict: an unmeasured endpoint is an untested part, not evidence of a limitation. Tables 1–3 and the appendices provide additional method and adaptation comparisons, but do not resolve the claim's terminal-fitting predictions. Random-label test accuracy is explicitly excluded in Appendix D.1.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures task accuracy on continually changing random-label tasks, but does not test zero or near-zero training error and chance test error for one fixed random labeling in the original supervised setting, or whether the original architecture and training hyperparameters are unchanged.
It does not compare training time to fit random labels versus true labels or measure convergence as the corrupted-label fraction changes.
Permuted MNIST uses true digit labels; the study does not test shuffled-pixel or Gaussian-noise inputs with random labels.
It does not sweep the fraction of corrupted labels from none to all or report the paired training and test error pattern.

Regularization baselines appear in continual-learning comparisons, but the study does not test whether explicit regularization prevents fitting random labels or whether removing it harms generalization on true labels.
It does not track whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: NeuMoSync
rows.operation_detail: Sequential training on tasks with randomly assigned CIFAR-10 labels; reports average online task accuracy.
rows.baseline: Baseline methods; no exact value stated in the accompanying text
rows.note: Authors state NeuMoSync performs best on the random-label tasks with a large gap, but the plotted value is not stated in the text. The continual task sequence and accuracy measure do not establish zero training error on one fixed random labeling.
rows.check: Average online task accuracy measures performance throughout training, not terminal fitting error. NeuMoSync includes a global controller and consolidated network beyond the stated MLP backbone. Its superiority over baselines does not demonstrate partial fulfillment of V1.

rows.subject: NeuMoSync
rows.operation_detail: Sequential training on tasks with randomly assigned MNIST labels; reports average online task accuracy.
rows.baseline: Baseline methods; no exact value stated in the accompanying text
rows.note: Authors state NeuMoSync performs best on the random-label tasks with a large gap, but the plotted value is not stated in the text. The continual task sequence and accuracy measure do not establish zero training error on one fixed random labeling.
rows.check: Average online task accuracy cannot determine whether training eventually reaches near-zero error. The stated MLP size describes only NeuMoSync's backbone. The figure-only comparison provides no basis for assigning partial fulfillment of V1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Random-label MNIST and CIFAR-10 continual-learning tasks
reader_labels.reason: The study reports accuracy on sequences of random-label tasks and says NeuMoSync outperforms the baselines, but does not report the zero-error and chance-test-error result specified by V1 (R1, R2).
